title: European Union threshold pack (drinking water, groundwater, nitrates, sewage sludge and soil, food, EFSA, bathing water)
legend: Same fields and vocabulary as ny-us.json. Member States transpose directives and may set stricter national values; a farm passport in a Member State must add the national pack (not covered here).

rows.applicability: point of compliance (DWD Art. 6); Member States use 'Sum of PFAS', 'PFAS Total' or both; private well — reference by analogy
rows.determination_rule: per national transposition and DWD monitoring rules; LOQ for the sum should be ≤ 30 ng/L
rows.source_doc: Directive (EU) 2020/2184, Annex I Part B; Commission technical guidelines C/2024/4910 on analytical methods for PFAS
rows.note: Compare only a complete 20-PFAS sum; a partial sum is a lower bound.

rows.applicability: as EU-01
rows.note: Includes TFA.

rows.unit: mg/L as NO3 (= 11.3 mg/L as N)
rows.applicability: as EU-01
rows.source_doc: Directive (EU) 2020/2184, Annex I Part B (value carried over from Directive 98/83/EC)
rows.note: EUR-Lex page fetched without the annex text. Unit is the NO3 ion — convert US 'as N' results with factor 4.427 before comparing.

rows.analyte: sum of 4 PFAS (PFHxS, PFOS, PFOA, PFNA)
rows.applicability: groundwater quality standard (Directive 2006/118/EC Annex I as amended)
rows.determination_rule: groundwater chemical status assessment under the WFD/GWD; good status by 22 Dec 2039
rows.note: EUR-Lex text read: recital 17 confirms a four-PFAS standard based on the EFSA value; the annex number itself was not in the retrieved text. Dates per Fieldfisher (in force 11 May 2026; PFAS standards apply from 22 Dec 2027).

rows.analyte: Sum of PFAS (20, aligned with the DWD)
rows.applicability: groundwater; dynamic alignment with the DWD parametric value
rows.source_doc: Directive (EU) 2026/805, recital 17 and amended Annex I of 2006/118/EC
rows.note: Alignment confirmed in the recital; numeric value via the DWD.

rows.analyte: sum of 25 PFAS (PFOA equivalents, incl. TFA)
rows.applicability: environmental quality standard (EQSD Annex I as amended)
rows.note: Value not retrieved in this check — row kept as a named gap of the pack.

rows.analyte: nitrate — 'polluted water' criterion for nitrate vulnerable zones
rows.applicability: designation of NVZs by Member States; a farm-level screening reference
rows.determination_rule: waters that contain or could contain more than 50 mg/L if no action is taken

rows.applicability: livestock manure only — NOT sewage sludge; derogations above 170 exist by Commission decision
rows.source_doc: Nitrates Directive Annex III point 2; Commission evaluation SWD(2026) 234, Annex XVII

rows.unit: mg/kg dry matter (range 1–3; national value within range)
rows.applicability: use of sludge prohibited where the national soil limit is exceeded (Art. 5); stricter where pH < 6 (Art. 8)
rows.determination_rule: representative sample of 25 cores per ≤5 ha, depth 25 cm (Annex II C); screening uses the lower end of the range
rows.source_org: European Union (text via legislation.gov.uk EU archive)
rows.note: Annex I values are excluded from delegated amendment (Art. 13), so the archived text is current.

rows.applicability: as EU-09
rows.note: Up to +50 % allowed on soils with pH consistently > 7.

rows.applicability: as EU-09
as EU-09
as EU-09
as EU-09
rows.note: No EU limit for chromium; no EU limit for PFAS in sludge.

rows.applicability: Member States choose Annex I B (sludge concentration + tonnage) or Annex I C (load)
rows.determination_rule: sludge analysed at least every six months (Annex II A)
rows.source_doc: 86/278/EEC Annex I B and I C
rows.note: Other metals in Annex I B/I C: Cu 1000–1750 / 12; Ni 300–400 / 3; Pb 750–1200 / 15; Zn 2500–4000 / 30; Hg 16–25 / 0.1 (mg/kg DM / kg/ha/yr).

rows.matrix: grassland and forage crops receiving sludge
rows.analyte: waiting period before grazing or forage harvest
rows.applicability: Member States set the period, never less than three weeks; 10 months for crops eaten raw in contact with soil
rows.determination_rule: date of application vs date of grazing / harvest
rows.note: Directly relevant to biosolids on forage fields.

rows.analyte: soil health descriptors; PFAS watch list
rows.applicability: Directive (EU) 2025/2360 on soil monitoring and resilience: transposition within 3 years (Dec 2028); indicative list of contaminants incl. relevant PFAS within 18 months (by mid-2027); non-binding target values and national trigger values
rows.determination_rule: none at EU level for PFAS concentrations
rows.note: There is no EU numeric PFAS value for agricultural soil at the check date — say so in the card instead of borrowing one.

rows.analyte: PFOS / PFOA / PFNA / PFHxS / sum of 4
rows.applicability: maximum levels — food above them may not be placed on the market
rows.note: Annex text not opened; values agree across BfR, Agilent and Eurofins summaries.

rows.matrix: meat of bovine animals, pigs and poultry
rows.analyte: PFOS / PFOA / PFNA / PFHxS / sum of 4
rows.applicability: as EU-18

rows.matrix: offal of bovine animals, sheep, pigs and poultry
rows.analyte: PFOS / PFOA / PFNA / PFHxS / sum of 4
rows.applicability: as EU-18
indicative level above which the causes of contamination should be investigated; NOT a maximum level — there is no EU maximum level for PFAS in milk
rows.source_doc: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2022/1431 on the monitoring of perfluoroalkyl substances in food
rows.source_org: European Commission (values via Eurofins, Luxembourg food-safety authority)
rows.note: Milk indicative levels: PFOS 0.020, PFOA 0.010, PFNA 0.050, PFHxS 0.060 µg/kg. Absence of an EU milk maximum level confirmed by the Swiss FSVO data documentation (Dec 2025). Convert ng/L to µg/kg with density 1.03 kg/L.

rows.applicability: as EU-21
rows.note: PFNA 0.050, PFHxS 0.060 µg/kg.

rows.matrix: fruits, vegetables, starchy roots and tubers
rows.applicability: as EU-21
rows.note: Wild fungi: PFOS 1.5 µg/kg.

rows.applicability: EFSA TWI — shared with the NY-US pack (row NYUS-10)

rows.analyte: E. coli — excellent / good (95th percentile), sufficient (90th percentile)
rows.unit: CFU/100 mL (excellent ≤500; good ≤1000; sufficient ≤900 at p90)
rows.applicability: designated bathing waters, classification over the assessment period; a farm stream — orientation only
rows.determination_rule: percentile evaluation over the season set (Annex II); a single sample cannot be classified
rows.source_org: European Union (text via legislation.gov.uk; EEA Eionet code list)
rows.note: Intestinal enterococci: 200 / 400 / 330.

rows.applicability: food business operators producing raw milk
rows.determination_rule: rolling geometric average over three months, at least one sample per month
rows.note: Archived EU text; current EUR-Lex consolidation not re-read in this check.
rows.source_doc: Regulation (EC) No 853/2004, Annex III, Section IX, Chapter I, point 3(a)(i)
rows.source_org: European Union (text via legislation.gov.uk EU archive, as at 31.12.2020)

rows.applicability: as EU-26
rows.determination_rule: rolling geometric average over two months, at least two samples per month
rows.source_doc: Regulation (EC) No 853/2004, Annex III, Section IX

rows.applicability: maximum level — food above it may not be placed on the market
rows.determination_rule: official control per Regulation (EU) 2023/915 and sampling rules
rows.note: EUR-Lex annex not retrieved in this check; value unchanged from Regulation (EC) 1881/2006, which 2023/915 replaced. The article dates the levels from 25 April 2023 (adoption); entry into force 25 May 2023 not re-read in the act.
rows.matrix: raw milk, heat-treated milk, milk for dairy products
rows.source_doc: Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915, Annex I, row 1.1.16 (raw milk, heat-treated milk and milk for the manufacture of milk-based products) — table reproduced in trade press
rows.source_org: European Commission (Annex row via Food Safety Magazine, 8 May 2023)

rows.applies_from: 2011 (Annex I as substituted by Regulation (EU) No 574/2011)
rows.applicability: EU maximum content of an undesirable substance in animal feed — compound feed for dairy cattle and calves (also dairy sheep, goats and their young, piglets, young poultry)
rows.determination_rule: maximum content relative to feed with 12 % moisture, per lot
rows.note: Consolidated EU text CELEX 02002L0032-20191128 read via legislation.gov.uk (EU text as at IP completion day). Other rows: feed materials 0.02 mg/kg; complementary and complete feed 0.01 mg/kg. Amendments after 2020 not checked on EUR-Lex.
rows.source_doc: Directive 2002/32/EC, Annex I, Section II (mycotoxins), aflatoxin B1 — compound feed for dairy cattle and calves

rows.applicability: BfR model: feed level at which food of animal origin stays below EU maximum levels on average; PFOA 6.5, PFHxS 3.7 µg/kg
rows.note: Derived model value, not a legal limit.
rows.source_doc: BfR, 'Feed is key to compliance with maximum PFAS levels in food of animal origin' (as reported by Food Safety Magazine)
rows.source_org: German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (via secondary)
